parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal passport/entry screening treats trans/nonbinary markers as invalid or suspect, risking denial, fraud findings, and detention; immigration/corrections custody documents severe abuse and conversion-therapy practices. State and federal facility rules impose birth-sex placement in government-funded and school settings; for minors, mandatory outing to parents. Local public-accommodation ordinances and court challenges offer partial relief but do not offset federal/state traveler-facing exposure. No routine execution or criminal presentation arrest in this division, so above severe 0.15; universal exclusions and documented custody harm place it High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports/visas must match sex assigned at birth; X markers are blocked. Mismatch or reasonable doubt can trigger case notes, refusal, additional evidence, or permanent fraud if material; reports of passports confiscated/blocked and travelers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; court challenges; legal-aid FAQs. No national sodomy statute; allied travel advisories signal external concern, not protection.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport mismatch can move administrative screening into visa denial/fraud; local nondiscrimination rules do not limit federal entry screening or case notes.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration detention reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse; national corrections uses state model for conversion therapy, cuts hair, removes hormones, denies care; custody risks if entry fraud or public-order issues.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate-crime statute exists nationally, but no documented trans-visitor release/compensation. Courts contest some orders; effect in custody uncertain.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy or care/minor investigation can lead to detention; federal corrections/immigration rules override state and local protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal EO bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities. State school/college law requires birth-certificate bathrooms/locker/shower/overnight; other mapped jurisdictions include trespass arrests.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State law lacks enforcement mechanism; 33 local public-accommodation ordinances; many jurisdictions have no mapped ban. School exemptions single-occupancy.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal/funded facility rules plus state school statutes create unavoidable birth-sex placement; local ordinances cannot cancel government/school restrictions.

care_services.exposure: Hostile care climate: minors' care/sports act contested; funding threats and records subpoenas. Adult visitor care restrictions not documented.
care_services.protection: January 2024 adult rules withdrawn; some orders enjoined; local ordinances may aid service access; emergency care not documented.
care_services.interaction: If minor seeks care or enrollment, contested state/federal rules may force disclosure and denial; adult HRT/emergency exposure remains uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Officials frame gender ideology as threat; athletes case-note cable; counterterrorism targets radical pro-trans violent groups; removal of materials and prosecutions of teachers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Document says counterterrorism won't target mere disagreement; litigation, municipal ordinances, and local protections remain partially operative.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat language informs entry/care/school enforcement but not direct criminal status for quiet visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors in schools/colleges forced into birth-sex facilities; school staff must out LGBTQ students to parents; guardian may need documents and disclosure.
minors_guardians.protection: No criminal enforcement for facility law; local nondiscrimination ordinances; care/sports ban re-enjoined but status uncertain.
minors_guardians.interaction: Enrollment, camps, overnight activities, or school visits can expose both minor and guardian to document checks and parental outing.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented trans-specific hate violence or police profiling against visitors; hostile climate may raise risk in some spaces.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law; state lacks gender-identity bias statute but 33 local ordinances cover services; response varies.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street incidents may be handled inconsistently; local protections help private lodging but not federal/state facilities or immigration custody.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unknown which court orders, school enforcement, county practices, or care rules are live; outed traveler may face cascading document/facility custody checks.
remedies_unknowns.protection: ACLU suit, legal-aid FAQ, local ordinances, litigation. Some remedies may not work against federal entry/facility/custody.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Protections are fragmented; state/local remedies cannot pre-empt federal screening, funded facilities, or immigration/corrections custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: In 0.15-A, visitors are routinely arrested for presentation with months of custody and capital uncertainty. This division lacks criminal gender-presentation arrest and enforcement, and passport/entry exposure often yields denial rather than automatic imprisonment; however immigration custody abuse and fraud permanence keep it near High Risk rather than above it.

0.25-C has birth-sex custody and visitor arrest. Here, national/federal birth-sex facilities, school outing, and documented immigration custody abuse are similar severe universal exposures, but there is no documented routine visitor arrest under the state facility law, so slightly higher.

0.35-A involves visitor register denial/exclusion without credible imprisonment. This regime includes that exclusion plus possible permanent fraud and severe detention/abuse, plus facility mandates, so lower than 0.35-A.

0.55-B is administrative secondary screening/refusal without detention or severe custody. Here severe immigration/corrections abuse and federal/state facility exclusions make the risk materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative traveler risk is cascading: a home passport mismatch triggers federal screening and possible visa fraud denial; if detention follows, federal immigration/corrections custody may impose birth-sex placement, hormone removal, and abuse. In schools and government-funded spaces, federal/state rules force birth-sex facilities, while minors face mandatory outing. Local ordinances and litigation can help private lodging or employment but cannot cancel federal entry, funded facilities, school designation, or custody rules. The result is universal, high-severity exposure tempered by no routine criminalization of quiet visitors.
